37287640.title: File:Bathymetry of the MH370 Search Area.webm

ImageDescription.value: Before the underwater search for MH370 could begin, it was necessary to accurately map the sea floor to ensure that the search is undertaken safely and effectively. Bathymetry survey vessels spent months at sea, scanning the sea floor with multibeam sonar to gather detailed, high-resolution data. The data has revealed many seabed features for the first time. This computer-animated ‘flythrough’ shows a visualisation of some of the sea floor terrain in the search area.
An earth globe turning into and icosahedron and then unfolding, thereby projecting earth creating a projection of a Dymaxion map.

Artist.value: See script and authors listed in details below.

160671706.title: File:Fly-through video showing sharp bathymetric structures in the Lacaze-Duthiers canyon (Ifremer 00746-85829).webm

ImageDescription.value:
The Lacaze-Duthiers canyon’s flanks were mapped using the H-ROV Ariane multibeam echosounder installed with a 45° angle (CALADU-2019 oceanographic cruise). High-resolution bathymetric data collected on the canyon’s flanks made it possible to highlight a series of sub-parallel structures identified as lithified sedimentary strata along which coral colonies grow.

General map is from EMODnet Bathymetry: https://www.emodnet-bathymetry.eu/

Credit.value: Fly-through video showing sharp bathymetric structures in the Lacaze-Duthiers canyon

Artist.value: Pere Puig

160662101.title: File:Mise en oeuvre du ROV Victor 6000 par L'Atalante (Ifremer 00641-75275).webm

ImageDescription.value:
Dedicated to scientific research in the field of oceanography, Victor is a ROV (Remotely operated Vehicle), capable of operating at depths of up to 6,000 meters, instrumented and modular, equipped with two manipulator arms, which produces very high-quality video and photos, and which can carry and operate various scientific equipment and tools. The lower part of the machine consists of an instrumented module that can be interchanged depending on the nature of the mission. It contains most of the instrumentation as well as a sample collection basket.

This modular system can also serve as a technological platform for new equipment.

To date, Victor has two different modules, one for sampling, another for measurements (equipped, among other sensors, with a multi-beam sounder).

Thus equipped, Victor can carry out: long-term reconnaissance of areas in construction site mode (100 x 100 km) or in road mode; fine bathymetry and/or physicochemical measurements; sample collection and handling of specific tools.

Designed primarily for scientific missions, Victor can be used for various tasks (assistance, wreck search, technological platform).

Credit.value: Mise en oeuvre du ROV Victor 6000 par L'Atalante

ImageDescription.value:
This visualization shows ocean surface currents around the world during the period from June 2005 through Decemeber 2007. The visualization does not include a narration or annotations; the goal was to use ocean flow data to create a simple, visceral experience.

This visualization was produced using NASA/JPL's computational model called Estimating the Circulation and Climate of the Ocean, Phase II or ECCO2.. ECCO2 is high resolution model of the global ocean and sea-ice. ECCO2 attempts to model the oceans and sea ice to increasingly accurate resolutions that begin to resolve ocean eddies and other narrow-current systems which transport heat and carbon in the oceans.The ECCO2 model simulates ocean flows at all depths, but only surface flows are used in this visualization. The dark patterns under the ocean represent the undersea bathymetry. Topographic land exaggeration is 20x and bathymetric exaggeration is 40x.

This video is public domain and can be downloaded at: http://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/vis/a000000/a003800/a003827/index.html

149586293.title: File:Seafloor bathymetry and biodiversity of Arafura Marine Park.webm

ImageDescription.value:
This flythrough highlights seabed environments within two areas of Arafura Marine Park offshore northern Australia; Money Shoal and Pillar Bank. Located 250 km to the northeast of Darwin within the Arafura Sea, the marine park extends to the limit of Australia’s exclusive economic zone, covering an area of 22,924 km2. Money Shoal is an isolated carbonate reef platform that rises from 70 m to shallow subtidal depths and supports a diverse coral and demersal fish community. The surrounding seabed comprises muddy substrate characterized by extensive fields of pockmark, interpreted as evidence for fluid escape from organic-rich sediment. Pillar Bank, in contrast, is representative of the deeper (150 – 200 m depths) outer shelf area of the marine park that supports sparse benthic communities of filter feeders on local outcrops of hard substrate, surrounded by expanses of muddy substrate. Demersal fish are also present, as observed using baited underwater cameras.

Bathymetry data and seafloor imagery for this flythrough was collected in November 2020 by Geoscience Australia (GA) and the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS) on board RV Solander during survey SOL7491/GA0366. Funding was provided by the Australian Government’s National Environmental Science Program (NESP) Marine Biodiversity Hub, with co-investment by GA and AIMS.

For further information see: Picard, K. et al. 2020. Arafura Marine Park Post Survey Report. www.nespmarine.edu.au

ImageDescription.value: Straddling the equator approximately 1000 kilometres to the west of the South American mainland, the Galapagos Islands lie within the heart of the equatorial current system. Rising from the sea floor, the volcanic islands of the Galapagos are set on top of a large submarine platform. The main portion of the Galapagos platform is relatively flat and less than 1000 meters in depth. The steepest slopes are found along the western and southern flanks of the platform with a gradual slope towards the east. The interactions of the Galapagos and the oceanic currents create vastly different environmental regimes which not only isolates one part of the Archipelago from the other but allows penguins to live along the equator on the western part of the Archipelago and tropical corals around the islands to the north. The islands are relatively new in geologic terms with the youngest islands in the west still exhibiting periodic eruptions from their massive volcanic craters.
